subject.title: [Feature]: Add a standard AISP/AISOP proposal contract for Skill Workshop

question: Should Skill Workshop lifecycle invariants become a maintained core contract artifact, and if so should that artifact be OpenClaw-native, AISP/AISOP reference-only, or moved to ClawHub?
rationale: The implementation shape determines security authority over scanner, approval, rollback, write-target, and surface-consistency rules; automation cannot safely choose whether a contract is documentation, test fixture, validator input, or runtime governance.

options.title: OpenClaw-native contract plus tests
options.body: Add a small core-owned docs/test fixture that mirrors current Skill Workshop invariants first, with AISP left as illustrative or generated later.

options.title: Reference artifact in ClawHub
options.body: Keep OpenClaw core on prose docs and runtime tests while publishing any AISP/AISOP package as an external skill or bundle artifact.

options.title: Defer contract standardization
options.body: Keep the existing docs and service tests as the authority until a concrete validator or lifecycle trace consumer needs a machine-readable schema.

recommendation.title: OpenClaw-native contract plus tests
recommendation.body: Add a small core-owned docs/test fixture that mirrors current Skill Workshop invariants first, with AISP left as illustrative or generated later.

likelyOwner.reason: This person authored the merged Skill Workshop foundation and is the best history-backed routing candidate for deciding the contract boundary.
